title: Package Architecture
text: TemporalHazard pure-R reimplementation C/SAS HAZARD procedure originally developed University Alabama Birmingham (UAB) multi-phase parametric hazard modeling (Blackstone, Naftel, Turner 1986). SAS/C code R package currently developed maintained Cleveland Clinic Foundation, R code wholly developed Cleveland Clinic Foundation. package provides unified framework fitting additive hazard models arbitrary number temporal phases, governed three-parameter decompos(t; t_half, nu, m) family. generalized temporal decomposition extends naturally longitudinal mixed-effects settings (Rajeswaran et al. 2018). vignette documents internal architecture: source files organized, functions compose fitting pipeline, golden fixtures ensure regression-free development, reference datasets ship package.

title: Package Architecture
text: primary user entry point hazard(), dispatches distribution-specific optimizers. diagram shows call flow multiphase fit. single-phase distributions (Weibull, exponential, log-logistic, log-normal), hazard() dispatches corresponding .hzr_optim_<dist>() function, calls .hzr_optim_generic() distribution-specific log-likelihood gradient. multiphase model concatenates per-phase sub-vectors single flat theta internal (estimation) scale: Internal theta layout per phase .hzr_split_theta() partitions concatenated vector named list per-phase sub-vectors. .hzr_unpack_phase_theta() extracts named parameters (log_mu, log_t_half, nu, m, beta) sub-vector. hzr_phase(type, t_half, nu, m, formula) creates lightweight S3 object stores phase type, initial shape parameters, optional phase-specific covariate formula. constructor validates inputs returns NA shape parameters constant phases. list hzr_phase objects validated .hzr_validate_phases(), auto-names unnamed phases (“phase_1”, “phase_2”, …) catches common mistake passing bare hzr_phase instead list. hzr_decompos(time, t_half, nu, m) mathematical core. computes G(t) (CDF), g(t) (density), h(t) (hazard) three-parameter family across six valid sign combinations nu m. phase-level helpers hzr_phase_cumhaz() hzr_phase_hazard() wrap hzr_decompos() apply phase type mapping: .hzr_optim_multiphase() runs multi-start strategy: first start uses assembled starting values (theta hzr_phase specs); subsequent starts perturb randomly (sd = 0.5). best log-likelihood across starts kept. helps optimizer escape shallow local optima common multiphase models. optimizer delegates .hzr_optim_generic(), wraps stats::optim() method "BFGS" (unconstrained; scale parameters log-transformed). Hessian computed numerically converged point variance-covariance estimation.

title: Package Architecture
text: TemporalHazard ships five clinical reference datasets inst/extdata/, converted original C/SAS HAZARD test data. datasets used vignette examples parity testing. Reference datasets (lazy-loaded via data()) AVC dataset contains 310 patients underwent repair atrioventricular septal defects. primary example dataset used throughout hazard modeling examples richest set covariates multivariable analysis. AVC dataset variables KUL dataset large series 5880 primary isolated CABG patients KU Leuven (1971–July 1987). serves primary benchmark C binary parity testing simplest structure (intercept-, right-censored) combined large sample size exercises three temporal phases. original SAS analysis (hz.deadp.KUL.sas) also includes return--angina reintervention endpoints (recorded original fixed-width file 6 columns), death endpoint (int_dead, dead) extracted parity testing. OMC dataset contains 339 patients unique collection involves repeated thromboembolic events (3 per patient) left censoring. SAS analysis transforms dataset repeated-events format using STARTTME CENSORED indicators, exercising interval censoring likelihood. TGA dataset contains 470 patients underwent arterial switch operation. includes derived variables (logarithmic inverse transforms clinical measurements) primarily used sensitivity analysis internal validation examples. VALVES dataset largest multivariable example 1533 patients multiple endpoints (death, prosthetic valve endocarditis, bioprosthesis degeneration, reoperation). SAS analysis (hm.deadp.VALVES.sas) fits multivariable 3-phase model 10 covariates across multiple event types.

title: Package Architecture
text: original C/SAS HAZARD procedure uses different parameterization TemporalHazard. hzr_argument_mapping() function documents full translation. SAS HAZARD R parameter mapping (excerpt) SAS early phase uses four parameters: DELTA, RHO (THALF), NU, M. collapse onto three-parameter decompos family: DELTA —Time transformation B(t) = (exp(delta*t) - 1)/delta. DELTA = 0 (common case), B(t) = t transformation absorbed. Non-zero DELTA currently supported. RHO / THALF —Scale parameter. RHO = NU * THALF * ((2^M - 1)/M)^NU. Maps directly t_half hzr_phase(). NU —Time exponent. Maps directly. M —Shape exponent. Maps directly. SAS late phase uses G3 decomposition four parameters, now directly supported via hzr_phase("g3", ...): TAU –> tau (scale parameter) GAMMA –> gamma (time exponent) ALPHA –> alpha (shape parameter; alpha = 0 gives exponential case) ETA –> eta (outer exponent) G3 formula (alpha > 0) : \(G_3(t) = \left(\left((t/\tau)^\gamma + 1\right)^{1/\alpha} - 1\right)^\eta\) Unlike G1, G3 unbounded —can grow without limit, making suitable late-phase rising hazards. KUL benchmark gamma = 3, alpha = 1, eta = 1, simplifies \(G_3(t) = t^3\).

title: Fitting Hazard Models
text: single-Weibull fits gave us curve ’s mediocre everywhere instead right anywhere. ’s structural limitation monotone parametric shape, something iterations fix. Blackstone–Naftel–Turner framework’s key idea split hazard sum phase-specific contributions, temporal shape scale: \[H(t \mid x) = \sum_{j=1}^{J} \mu_j(x) \cdot \Phi_j(t)\] \(\Phi_j(t)\) phase-specific unit-scaled curve (early-peaking saturating, flat constant, late-rising polynomial) \(\mu_j(x)\) phase-specific scale, possibly modulated covariates. phases overlap add — switching, thresholds — total instantaneous hazard \(t\) sum per-phase rates. See vignette("getting-started") longer-form motivation; follows practical workflow fitting one. AVC ’ll use two phases — early phase absorb operative-window mortality, constant phase background rate. AVC patients don’t clear late-deterioration regime follow-window, third (g3) phase unidentified. fix shape parameters estimate scales, matching workflow ’d run SAS HAZARD reference fit. diagnostic matters whether multiphase fit actually -performs single Weibull data. Plot parametric curves Kaplan-Meier reference can see, eye, model honest reaching. Figure 2: Single-phase Weibull vs. multiphase model Kaplan-Meier (AVC) multiphase model tracks KM curve much closely single Weibull, especially across steep early-mortality window — exactly single Weibull forced compromise. constant phase carries slow post-recovery attrition. point isn’t multiphase always wins; ’s data phase structure, fitting structure explicitly strictly honest averaging away one monotone curve.

cdf (early risk) #>   phase 2:      constant - constant (flat rate) #>   engine:       native-r-m2  #>   converged:    TRUE  #>   log-lik:      -228.029  #>   evaluations: fn=32, gr=10 #>  #> Coefficients (internal scale): #>  #>   Phase: early (cdf) #>                estimate std_error    z_stat     p_value #>   log_mu     -1.4132735 0.1290435 -10.95192 6.50568e-28 #>   log_t_half -0.6931472        NA        NA          NA #>   nu          1.0000000        NA        NA          NA #>   m           1.0000000        NA        NA          NA #>  #>   Phase: constant (constant) #>           estimate std_error    z_stat      p_value #>   log_mu -7.609476 0.4495827 -16.92564 2.911483e-64 t_grid <- seq(0.01, max(avc$int_dead) * 0.95, length.out = 200) nd     <- data.frame(time = t_grid)  km_avc <- survfit(Surv(int_dead, dead) ~ 1, data = avc) km_df  <- data.frame(time = km_avc$time, survival = km_avc$surv * 100)  fit_wb <- hazard(   Surv(int_dead, dead) ~ 1, data = avc, dist = "weibull",   theta = c(mu = 0.20, nu = 1.0), fit = TRUE )  surv_wb <- predict(fit_wb, newdata = nd, type = "survival") * 100 surv_mp <- predict(fit_mp, newdata = nd, type = "survival") * 100  plot_df <- rbind(   data.frame(time = t_grid, survival = surv_wb, Model = "Single Weibull"),   data.frame(time = t_grid, survival = surv_mp, Model = "Multiphase (2-phase)") )  ggplot() +   geom_step(data = km_df, aes(time, survival), colour = "grey50",             linewidth = 0.5) +   geom_line(data = plot_df, aes(time, survival, colour = Model),             linewidth = 1) +   scale_colour_manual(values = c("Single Weibull" = "#E69F00",                                  "Multiphase (2-phase)" = "#0072B2")) +   scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +   annotate("text", x = max(t_grid) * 0.6, y = 95, label = "KM (grey)",            size = 3, colour = "grey50") +   labs(x = "Months after AVC repair", y = "Freedom from death (%)",        colour = NULL) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

title: Fitting Hazard Models
text: Right censoring far common censoring type clinical survival data — patient still alive last follow-, know event time exceeds observed window. Two types arise frequently enough warrant explicit handling. Interval censoring occurs event known happened two observation times, specific time. canonical example clinic-visit data: patient confirmed alive month 12 found dead month 24, event occurred somewhere \((12, 24)\). naive analysis treats event right-censored 12 exactly observed 24; introduce bias. Left censoring mirror: event occurred first observation time (time_upper), already established moment first contact — \(T \leq t_{\text{upper}}\). package encodes censoring type status vector: interval-censored rows, supply time_lower time_upper. can pass direct arguments hazard(), hand Surv() object instead: Surv(lower, upper, event, type = "interval") Surv(lower, upper, type = "interval2") work, Surv(time, event, type = "left") left censoring Surv(start, stop, event) counting-process (repeating-event) data. One thing watch, two interfaces use numbers. table package’s coding, pass status argument. Surv() scheme — type = "interval" reads 0 right-censored, 1 exact event, 2 left-censored 3 interval-censored — hazard() translates parses formula. use whichever coding belongs interface writing , don’t carry one set codes across . simulate 400 cardiac surgery patients observed semi-annual clinic visits (every 6 months, 4–8 scheduled visits per patient). event falls two consecutive visits observation interval-censored; falls last visit patient right-censored. Note time_lower counting-process entry time. Weibull multiphase likelihoods, time_lower doubles entry (left-truncation) time right-censored exact-event rows (status %% c(0, 1)): 0 < time_lower < time, row contributes H(stop) − H(start), counting-process form used epoch-decomposed repeated events. ordinary right-censored event row entry time, leave time_lower 0 omit . Setting time_lower = time treated entry — time_lower acts entry time strictly less time, longer zeroes row’s contribution. exponential, log-logistic, log-normal likelihoods use time_lower entry time unaffected. Fit Weibull model using censoring types: naive analyst doesn’t visit-bracket data record death discovery visit (time_upper) rather interval. overstates event time — patient appears survived longer — biasing estimated hazard shape. interval-censored fit recovers parameters accurately. naive fit estimates \(\mu\) comparably introduces substantial positive bias \(\nu\) — sees events consistently appearing visit times (every 6 months) infers sharper, periodic hazard shape doesn’t match underlying exponential structure.
code: set.seed(101) n         <- 400 visit_gap <- 6   # months between visits  # True event times: Weibull mu = 0.025, nu = 1.0 (median ~28 months) true_time <- rexp(n, rate = 0.025)  # nu=1 → exponential  n_visits  <- sample(4:8, n, replace = TRUE)  status     <- integer(n) time       <- numeric(n) time_lower <- numeric(n) time_upper <- numeric(n)  for (i in seq_len(n)) {   visits <- seq(visit_gap, n_visits[i] * visit_gap, by = visit_gap)   t_ev   <- true_time[i]   brk    <- findInterval(t_ev, c(0, visits))  # which interval contains t_ev    if (brk > length(visits)) {     # Event after last visit: right-censored.     # time_lower = 0: with H(time_lower) = H(0) = 0, the right-censored     # contribution reduces to -(H(time) - H(0)) = -H(time), which is correct.     status[i]     <- 0L     time[i]       <- max(visits)     time_lower[i] <- 0     time_upper[i] <- max(visits)   } else {     # Event within the visit window: interval-censored in (lower, upper)     lower_bound   <- if (brk == 1L) 0 else visits[brk - 1L]     upper_bound   <- visits[brk]     status[i]     <- 2L     time[i]       <- lower_bound     time_lower[i] <- lower_bound     time_upper[i] <- upper_bound   } }  table(status) #> status #>   0   2  #> 168 232 fit_ic <- hazard(   time       = time,   status     = status,   time_lower = time_lower,   time_upper = time_upper,   dist  = "weibull",   theta = c(mu = 0.025, nu = 1.0),   fit   = TRUE )  fit_ic #> hazard object #>   observations: 400  #>   predictors:   0  #>   dist:         weibull  #>   engine:       native-r-m2  #>   log-lik:      -674.374  #>   converged:    TRUE # Naive: treat each interval-censored row as an exact event at time_upper # (the visit when the death was first recorded) fit_naive <- hazard(   time   = ifelse(status == 2L, time_upper, time),   status = ifelse(status == 2L, 1L,         status),   dist  = "weibull",   theta = c(mu = 0.025, nu = 1.0),   fit   = TRUE )  # Compare MLEs; true parameters are mu = 0.025, nu = 1.0 rbind(   interval_censored = round(coef(fit_ic)[1:2],   4),   naive_exact_upper = round(coef(fit_naive)[1:2], 4),   truth             = c(mu = 0.025, nu = 1.0) ) #>                       mu     nu #> interval_censored 0.0251 1.0345 #> naive_exact_upper 0.0259 1.4566 #> truth             0.0250 1.0000

Such a phase has not started by the end of follow-up, so #> neither its 'mu' nor its shape is identified: the fit converges and those #> parameters drift freely.  # Scale magnitudes: exp(log_mu) ≈ 0 for any phase the data doesn't support log_mu_idx <- grep("log_mu", names(coef(fit_3ph))) round(exp(coef(fit_3ph)[log_mu_idx]), 6) #>    early.log_mu constant.log_mu     late.log_mu  #>        0.248871        0.000000        0.000006 set.seed(42) fit_robust <- hazard(   Surv(int_dead, dead) ~ 1,   data   = avc,   dist   = "multiphase",   phases = list(     early    = hzr_phase("cdf", t_half = 0.5, nu = 1, m = 1,                           fixed = "shapes"),     constant = hzr_phase("constant")   ),   fit     = TRUE,   control = list(n_starts = 10, maxit = 1000) ) fit_robust$fit$converged #> [1] TRUE

title: Fitting Hazard Models
text: ’ve now seen phase type use: "cdf" early phase AVC operative mortality, "constant" phase AVC background rate, implicit single shape every Weibull fit. package supports three phase types total, summarized quick reference: "cdf" type covers widest range shapes: setting t_half small (e.g., 0.5) creates early-peaking phase; setting large (e.g., 10) creates late-rising phase. "constant" phase needs shape parameters. "g3" shape explicit late-rising parameterization matches SAS HAZARD “late” library; use need parity C/SAS reference fit, late rise clear lag--accelerate pattern delayed "cdf" doesn’t capture cleanly. See vignette("mf-mathematical-foundations") full mathematical treatment , including parameter identifiability constraints.

title: Getting Started with TemporalHazard
text: simulated data 180 patients three plausible risk covariates — age, NYHA functional class, cardiogenic shock. fit single Weibull hazard: scale parameter (mu) shape exponent (nu) lets hazard accelerate nu > 1, decelerate nu < 1, stay flat nu = 1. Weibull natural starting point single-distribution fit covers three monotone shapes just two parameters. hazard() interface takes survival formula (Surv(time, status) left, covariates right), starting-value vector (theta), distribution name. Passing fit = TRUE runs optimizer returns fitted model; passing fit = FALSE returns model specification without fitting, useful sanity-checking formula starting values committing optimizer.
code: library(TemporalHazard) library(survival)  set.seed(1001) n <- 180 dat <- data.frame(   time = rexp(n, rate = 0.35) + 0.05,   status = rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = 0.6),   age = rnorm(n, mean = 62, sd = 11),   nyha = sample(1:4, n, replace = TRUE),   shock = rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = 0.18) )  fit <- TemporalHazard::hazard(   Surv(time, status) ~ age + nyha + shock,   data = dat,   theta = c(mu = 0.25, nu = 1.10, beta1 = 0, beta2 = 0, beta3 = 0),   dist = "weibull",   fit = TRUE,   control = list(maxit = 300) )  summary(fit) #> hazard model summary #>   observations: 180  #>   predictors:   3  #>   dist:         weibull  #>   engine:       native-r-m2  #>   converged:    TRUE  #>   log-lik:      -293.553  #>   evaluations: fn=36, gr=8 #>  #> Coefficients: #>          estimate   std_error      z_stat      p_value #> mu    0.121860518 0.062260593  1.95726560 5.031625e-02 #> nu    1.143730632 0.084302528 13.56697905 6.285984e-42 #> beta1 0.001716551 0.008807986  0.19488579 8.454824e-01 #> beta2 0.156208724 0.090597558  1.72420458 8.467092e-02 #> beta3 0.017352702 0.362918430  0.04781433 9.618642e-01

title: Getting Started with TemporalHazard
text: fitted hazard model lets score new patients without refitting. predict() method takes newdata frame type argument selects quantity compute: "linear_predictor" — covariate-driven log-hazard-ratio row, \(x^\top \beta\). "hazard" — hazard multiplier, \(\exp(x^\top \beta)\). "survival" — probability surviving past row’s time, \(S(t \mid x)\). "cumulative_hazard" — integrated hazard row’s time, \(H(t \mid x) = -\log S(t \mid x)\). three rows made-patients spanning covariate range training data: younger, low-NYHA, -shock patient early time; middle case median; older, high-NYHA, shock patient . compute four prediction types .
code: new_patients <- data.frame(   time = c(0.5, 1.5, 3.0),   age = c(50, 65, 75),   nyha = c(1, 3, 4),   shock = c(0, 0, 1) )  pred_input <- new_patients  new_patients$linear_predictor <- predict(fit, newdata = pred_input, type = "linear_predictor") new_patients$hazard_multiplier <- predict(fit, newdata = pred_input, type = "hazard") new_patients$survival <- predict(fit, newdata = pred_input, type = "survival") new_patients$cumulative_hazard <- predict(fit, newdata = pred_input, type = "cumulative_hazard")  new_patients #>   time age nyha shock linear_predictor hazard_multiplier  survival #> 1  0.5  50    1     0        0.2420363          1.273840 0.9494097 #> 2  1.5  65    3     0        0.5802020          1.786399 0.7743185 #> 3  3.0  75    4     1        0.7709289          2.161774 0.5046535 #>   cumulative_hazard #> 1        0.05191482 #> 2        0.25577202 #> 3        0.68388317

text: package ships small set numerical helpers used internally keep likelihood evaluations stable across wide range arguments optimizer encounters. ’re exported can reach custom code debugging fit. common one hzr_log1pexp(x), computes \(\log(1 + e^x)\) numerically stable way. naive log(1 + exp(x)) overflows \(x\) exceeds 700 (exp(x) overflows); helper switches asymptotic \(x + \log(1 + e^{-x})\) large \(x\), exact floating-point precision. package uses inside every log-likelihood expression involves log-survival term, evaluation can run \(x = -50\) \(x = 5000\) without producing Inf NaN.

code: data(avc) avc <- na.omit(avc)  # Candidate covariates candidates <- c("age", "status", "mal", "com_iv", "inc_surg", "orifice") logit_fits <- lapply(candidates, function(var) {   fmla <- as.formula(paste("dead ~", var))   glm(fmla, data = avc, family = binomial()) }) names(logit_fits) <- candidates  # Which covariates are significant univariably? p_values <- vapply(logit_fits, function(f) {   coef(summary(f))[2, "Pr(>|z|)"] }, numeric(1))  data.frame(covariate = names(p_values),            p_value   = round(p_values, 4),            row.names = NULL) #>   covariate p_value #> 1       age  0.0017 #> 2    status  0.0000 #> 3       mal  0.0006 #> 4    com_iv  0.0000 #> 5  inc_surg  0.0114 #> 6   orifice  0.0034 ggplot(avc, aes(age, dead)) +   geom_jitter(height = 0.05, width = 0, alpha = 0.3, size = 1) +   geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE, colour = "#0072B2",               linewidth = 0.8) +   labs(x = "Age at operation (months)", y = "Death (0/1)") +   theme_minimal() #> `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x' age_cal <- hzr_calibrate(   x      = avc$age,   event  = avc$dead,   groups = 10,   link   = "logit" ) print(age_cal) #> Variable calibration (logit link, 10 groups) #>  #>  group  n events    mean     min     max  prob link_value #>      1 30     11   3.519   1.051   5.388 0.367     -0.547 #>      2 31     11   8.665   5.421  11.532 0.355     -0.598 #>      3 30     13  15.194  11.631  18.497 0.433     -0.268 #>      4 31     11  23.077  18.990  27.828 0.355     -0.598 #>      5 30      7  43.544  28.124  57.167 0.233     -1.190 #>      6 31      3  72.066  59.730  86.408 0.097     -2.234 #>      7 30      2 101.154  86.507 117.522 0.067     -2.639 #>      8 31      3 162.739 121.169 203.733 0.097     -2.234 #>      9 30      4 247.051 205.343 297.140 0.133     -1.872 #>     10 31      3 530.623 324.573 790.981 0.097     -2.234

title: Inference & Diagnostics
text: delta-method CIs predict(se.fit = TRUE) returns fast asymptotically correct, lean Hessian-derived parameter vcov — can mislead likelihood surface poorly behaved near MLE (boundary fits, near-degenerate parameter combinations, small samples). package flags cases : fit carries rcond, pd weak diagnostics, summary() prints note (matching warning fit time) Hessian ill-conditioned, positive-definite, inverted , flat along combination parameters — strong signal prefer bootstrap. last one worth reading closely: means individual estimates along direction pinned data, standard errors unreliable. Bootstrap resampling robust alternative: refit model resampled dataset, collect resulting parameter prediction values, read empirical 2.5th / 97.5th percentiles 95% CI. ’s computationally heavier doesn’t assume likelihood locally quadratic, picks right tail behavior even delta-method theory creaks. hzr_bootstrap() wraps resample--refit loop corresponds SAS bootstrap.hazard.sas bootstrap.summary.sas macros. fit base model first; bootstrap replicates resample data refit using starting values. hzr_bootstrap() returns long data frame per-replicate coefficient estimates ($replicates) parameter-level summary (mean, SD, 95% percentile CI) $summary. use n_boot = 30 purely vignette renders reasonable time — real analysis ’d want 200 replicates. set.seed(42) call hzr_bootstrap() makes resample sequence reproducible. parameter-level CIs come directly bootstrap distribution. Prediction-level CIs (survival curve hazard profile) require pivoting boot$replicates wide format evaluating parametric survival formula per replicate. workflow scope section, building blocks returned object.
code: # Fit the base model that bootstrapping will use fit <- hazard(   Surv(int_dead, dead) ~ age + status + mal + com_iv,   data  = avc,   dist  = "weibull",   theta = c(mu = 0.20, nu = 1.0, rep(0, 4)),   fit   = TRUE,   control = list(maxit = 500) )  # Prediction grid at a median-risk profile t_grid <- seq(0.01, max(avc$int_dead) * 0.9, length.out = 100) base_nd <- data.frame(time = t_grid, age = median(avc$age),                       status = 2, mal = 0, com_iv = 0)  surv_point <- predict(fit, newdata = base_nd, type = "survival") set.seed(42) boot <- hzr_bootstrap(fit, n_boot = 30)  # kept small for vignette build time print(boot) #> Bootstrap inference for hazard model #> Mode: fixed refit  #> Replicates: 30 successful, 0 failed #>  #>  parameter  n pct    mean     sd     min    max ci_lower ci_upper #>         mu 30 100  0.0000 0.0000  0.0000 0.0000   0.0000   0.0000 #>         nu 30 100  0.2174 0.0603  0.0004 0.2668   0.0012   0.2587 #>        age 30 100 -0.0025 0.0024 -0.0100 0.0026  -0.0079   0.0011 #>     status 30 100  0.6778 0.1666  0.2712 1.0751   0.3792   0.9582 #>        mal 30 100  0.4165 0.3526 -0.4065 0.9703  -0.3595   0.9447 #>     com_iv 30 100  0.9099 0.4358  0.0609 2.0954   0.2661   2.0265

title: Mathematical Foundations of TemporalHazard

Every temporal phase TemporalHazard built single parametric family, decompos(t; t_half, nu, m), introduced Blackstone, Naftel, Turner (1986) produces three linked quantities just three parameters: \(G(t)\) — cumulative distribution function (CDF), bounded \([0, 1]\) \(g(t) = dG/dt\) — probability density function \(h(t) = g(t) / (1 - G(t))\) — hazard function three parameters control shape distribution: SAS/C parameter bridge original C code used different parameter names per phase: Early phase (G1): DELTA, RHO/THALF, NU, M \(\) t_half, nu, m Late phase (G3): TAU, GAMMA, ALPHA, ETA \(\) t_half, nu, m collapse onto 3-parameter decomposition family. C DELTA parameter controlled time transformation \(B(t) = (\exp(\delta t) - 1)/\delta\) absorbed shape. R, hzr_decompos() computes three quantities: Different sign combinations \(
u\) \(m\) pick different asymptotic behaviors decompos(), package treats separate case numerical stability. combination \(m < 0\) \(
u < 0\) produces integrand finite normalization rejected input-validation step. remaining six catalog every phase package selects : Six valid parameter sign combinations following plot shows CDF \(G(t)\), density \(g(t)\), hazard \(h(t)\) case, t_half = 3: Figure 1: G(t), g(t), h(t) six valid decomposition cases construction begins rate function \(ho\) chosen \(G(t_{1/2}) = 0.5\) exactly. Case 1 (\(m > 0, 
u > 0\)): \[ ho = 
u \, t_{1/2} \left( rac{2^m - 1}{m}ight)^{\!
u} \] , dimensionless time \(b(t) = 
u t / ho\): \[ G(t) = \left(1 + m \, b(t)^{-1/
u}ight)^{-1/m} \] \[ g(t) = \left(1 + m \, b(t)^{-1/
u}ight)^{-1/m - 1}        \cdot b(t)^{-1/
u - 1} / ho \] five cases arise limits (\(m \0\), \(

code: t_grid <- seq(0.01, 10, length.out = 200)  # Standard sigmoidal (Case 1: m > 0, nu > 0) d <- hzr_decompos(t_grid, t_half = 3, nu = 2, m = 1)  # Verify the half-life property: G(t_half) = 0.5 d_half <- hzr_decompos(3, t_half = 3, nu = 2, m = 1) cat("G(t_half) =", round(d_half$G, 6), "\n") #> G(t_half) = 0.5  # Verify the identity: h(t) = g(t) / (1 - G(t)) h_check <- d$g / (1 - d$G) cat("Max |h - g/(1-G)| =", max(abs(d$h - h_check)), "\n") #> Max |h - g/(1-G)| = 0 if (has_ggplot) {   library(ggplot2)    params <- list(     "Case 1: m=1, nu=2"     = list(nu = 2,   m = 1),     "Case 1L: m=0, nu=2"    = list(nu = 2,   m = 0),     "Case 2: m=-0.5, nu=2"  = list(nu = 2,   m = -0.5),     "Case 2L: m=-0.5, nu=0" = list(nu = 0,   m = -0.5),     "Case 3: m=1, nu=-0.5"  = list(nu = -0.5, m = 1),     "Case 3L: m=0, nu=-0.5" = list(nu = -0.5, m = 0)   )    t_grid <- seq(0.01, 10, length.out = 200)   rows <- list()    for (nm in names(params)) {     p <- params[[nm]]     d <- hzr_decompos(t_grid, t_half = 3, nu = p$nu, m = p$m)     rows <- c(rows, list(data.frame(       time = rep(t_grid, 3),       value = c(d$G, d$g, d$h),       quantity = rep(c("G(t) — CDF", "g(t) — density", "h(t) — hazard"),                      each = length(t_grid)),       case = nm     )))   }    df <- do.call(rbind, rows)    # Cap hazard display at reasonable values for readability   df$value[df$quantity == "h(t) — hazard" & df$value > 5] <- NA    ggplot(df, aes(x = time, y = value)) +     geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +     facet_grid(quantity ~ case, scales = "free_y") +     labs(x = "Time", y = NULL) +     theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +     theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7)) }

title: Mathematical Foundations of TemporalHazard
text: total cumulative hazard decomposes additively across \(J\) phases: \[ H(t \mid \mathbf{x}) = \sum_{j=1}^{J} \mu_j(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \Phi_j(t;\, t_{1/2,j},\, \nu_j,\, m_j) \] : \(\mu_j(\mathbf{x}) = \exp(\alpha_j + \mathbf{x}_j \boldsymbol{\beta}_j)\) phase-specific log-linear scale covariates \(\Phi_j(t)\) temporal shape, determined phase type three phase types correspond different uses decomposition output: SAS/C bridge classic three-phase HAZARD model used: G1 (early) \(\\) hzr_phase("cdf", ...) G2 (constant) \(\\) hzr_phase("constant") G3 (late) \(\\) hzr_phase("hazard", ...) TemporalHazard generalizes \(N\) phases type. cumulative hazard, instantaneous hazard survival : \[ h(t \mid \mathbf{x}) = \sum_{j=1}^{J} \mu_j(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \varphi_j(t) \qquad\text{} \varphi_j = d\Phi_j/dt \] \[ S(t \mid \mathbf{x}) = \exp\!\bigl(-H(t \mid \mathbf{x})\bigr) \] derivative \(\varphi_j(t)\) depends phase type: "cdf": \(\varphi(t) = g(t)\) (density) "hazard": \(\varphi(t) = h(t) = g(t)/(1 - G(t))\) "constant": \(\varphi(t) = 1\) math exposed R hzr_phase(), builds one phase time, hazard(), composes phases full model. (t_half, nu, m) triple decompos() parameterizes "cdf" "hazard" shapes; "g3" shape exposes (tau, gamma, alpha, eta) parameters SAS “late” library; "constant" shape parameters . canonical three-phase model uses "cdf" shape early phase, "constant" background, either delayed "cdf" "g3" late phase. cumulative hazard contribution \(\Phi(t)\) instantaneous hazard \(\varphi(t)\) phase can computed directly: Figure 2: Phi(t) phi(t) phase type build intuition, three phases combine total hazard. key insight phases contribute additively cumulative hazard \(H(t)\), survival directly. Figure 3: Three-phase additive cumulative hazard: total = early + constant + late
code: # Classic three-phase pattern early <- hzr_phase("cdf",      t_half = 0.5, nu = 2, m = 0) const <- hzr_phase("constant") late  <- hzr_phase("hazard",   t_half = 5,   nu = 1, m = 0)  print(early) #> <hzr_phase> cdf (early risk)  #>   t_half = 0.5  nu = 2  m = 0 print(const) #> <hzr_phase> constant (flat rate) print(late) #> <hzr_phase> hazard (late risk)  #>   t_half = 5  nu = 1  m = 0 if (has_ggplot) {   t_grid <- seq(0.01, 12, length.out = 200)    phi_early <- hzr_phase_cumhaz(t_grid, t_half = 0.5, nu = 2, m = 0,                                  type = "cdf")   phi_late  <- hzr_phase_cumhaz(t_grid, t_half = 5, nu = 1, m = 0,                                  type = "hazard")   phi_const <- hzr_phase_cumhaz(t_grid, type = "constant")    dphi_early <- hzr_phase_hazard(t_grid, t_half = 0.5, nu = 2, m = 0,                                   type = "cdf")   dphi_late  <- hzr_phase_hazard(t_grid, t_half = 5, nu = 1, m = 0,                                   type = "hazard")   dphi_const <- hzr_phase_hazard(t_grid, type = "constant")    df <- data.frame(     time = rep(t_grid, 6),     value = c(phi_early, phi_late, phi_const,               dphi_early, dphi_late, dphi_const),     phase = rep(rep(c("cdf (early)", "hazard (late)", "constant"),                     each = length(t_grid)), 2),     quantity = rep(c("Phi(t) — cumulative", "phi(t) — instantaneous"),                    each = 3 * length(t_grid))   )    ggplot(df, aes(x = time, y = value, colour = phase)) +     geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +     facet_wrap(~ quantity, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +     scale_colour_manual(values = c(       "cdf (early)" = "#0072B2",       "hazard (late)" = "#D55E00",       "constant" = "#009E73"     )) +     labs(x = "Time", y = NULL, hzr_phase_cumhaz(t_grid, type = "constant")   H_late  <- mu_late  * hzr_phase_cumhaz(t_grid, t_half = 5, nu = 1,                                            m = 0, type = "hazard")   H_total <- H_early + H_const + H_late    df <- data.frame(     time = rep(t_grid, 4),     cumhaz = c(H_early, H_const, H_late, H_total),     component = rep(c("Early (cdf)", "Constant", "Late (hazard)", "Total"), component,                  linewidth = component)) +     geom_line() +     scale_colour_manual(values = c(       "Total" = "black", "Early (cdf)" = "#0072B2",       "Constant" = "#009E73", "Late (hazard)" = "#D55E00"     )) +     scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(       "Total" = 1.2, "Early (cdf)" = 0.6,       "Constant" = 0.6, "Late (hazard)" = 0.6     )) +     labs(x = "Time", y = code: # Classic three-phase pattern early <- hzr_phase("cdf",      t_half = 0.5, nu = 2, m = 0) const <- hzr_phase("constant") late  <- hzr_phase("hazard",   t_half = 5,   nu = 1, m = 0)  print(early) #> <hzr_phase> cdf (early risk)  #>   t_half = 0.5  nu = 2  m = 0 print(const) #> <hzr_phase> constant (flat rate) print(late) #> <hzr_phase> hazard (late risk)  #>   t_half = 5  nu = 1  m = 0 if (has_ggplot) {   t_grid <- seq(0.01, 12, length.out = 200)    phi_early <- hzr_phase_cumhaz(t_grid, t_half = 0.5, nu = 2, m = 0,                                  type = "cdf")   phi_late  <- hzr_phase_cumhaz(t_grid, t_half = 5, nu = 1, m = 0,                                  type = "hazard")   phi_const <- hzr_phase_cumhaz(t_grid, type = "constant")    dphi_early <- hzr_phase_hazard(t_grid, t_half = 0.5, nu = 2, m = 0,                                   type = "cdf")   dphi_late  <- hzr_phase_hazard(t_grid, t_half = 5, nu = 1, m = 0,                                   type = "hazard")   dphi_const <- hzr_phase_hazard(t_grid, type = "constant")    df <- data.frame(     time = rep(t_grid, 6),     value = c(phi_early, phi_late, phi_const,               dphi_early, dphi_late, dphi_const),     phase = rep(rep(c("cdf (early)", "hazard (late)", "constant"),                     each = length(t_grid)), 2),     quantity = rep(c("Phi(t) — cumulative", "phi(t) — instantaneous"),                    each = 3 * length(t_grid))   )    ggplot(df, aes(x = time, y = value, colour = phase)) +     geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +     facet_wrap(~ quantity, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +     scale_colour_manual(values = c(       "cdf (early)" = "#0072B2",       "hazard (late)" = "#D55E00",       "constant" = "#009E73"     )) +     labs(x = "Time", y = NULL, colour = "Phase type") +     theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +     theme(legend.position = "bottom") }

code: if (has_ggplot) {   t_grid <- seq(0.01, 15, length.out = 300)    mu_early <- 0.3   mu_const <- 0.05   mu_late  <- 0.2    H_early <- mu_early * hzr_phase_cumhaz(t_grid, t_half = 0.5, nu = 2,                                            m = 0, type = "cdf")   H_const <- mu_const * hzr_phase_cumhaz(t_grid, type = "constant")   H_late  <- mu_late  * hzr_phase_cumhaz(t_grid, t_half = 5, nu = 1,                                            m = 0, type = "hazard")   H_total <- H_early + H_const + H_late    df <- data.frame(     time = rep(t_grid, 4),     cumhaz = c(H_early, H_const, H_late, H_total),     component = rep(c("Early (cdf)", "Constant", "Late (hazard)", "Total"),                     each = length(t_grid))   )   df$component <- factor(df$component,     levels = c("Total", "Early (cdf)", "Constant", "Late (hazard)"))    ggplot(df, aes(x = time, y = cumhaz, colour = component,                  linewidth = component)) +     geom_line() +     scale_colour_manual(values = c(       "Total" = "black", "Early (cdf)" = "#0072B2",       "Constant" = "#009E73", "Late (hazard)" = "#D55E00"     )) +     scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(       "Total" = 1.2, "Early (cdf)" = 0.6,       "Constant" = 0.6, "Late (hazard)" = 0.6     )) +     labs(x = "Time", y = "Cumulative hazard H(t)",          colour = NULL, linewidth = NULL) +     theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +     theme(legend.position = "bottom") }

code: data(cabgkul)  fit_mp <- hazard(   Surv(int_dead, dead) ~ 1,   data   = cabgkul,   dist   = "multiphase",   phases = list(     early    = hzr_phase("cdf", t_half = 0.2, nu = 1, m = 1,                           fixed = "shapes"),     constant = hzr_phase("constant"),     late     = hzr_phase("g3",  tau = 1, gamma = 3, alpha = 1, eta = 1,                           fixed = "shapes")   ),   fit     = TRUE,   control = list(n_starts = 5, maxit = 1000) ) t_mp <- seq(0.01, max(cabgkul$int_dead) * 0.95, length.out = 200) nd   <- data.frame(time = t_mp)  decomp <- predict(fit_mp, newdata = nd, type = "cumulative_hazard",                   decompose = TRUE)  # Numerical differentiation: h(t) ≈ ΔH(t) / Δt num_hazard <- function(cumhaz, time) {   dt <- diff(time)   dH <- diff(cumhaz)   c(dH[1] / dt[1], dH / dt) }  h_long <- rbind(   data.frame(time = t_mp, hazard = num_hazard(decomp$early, t_mp),              Phase = "Early"),   data.frame(time = t_mp, hazard = num_hazard(decomp$constant, t_mp),              Phase = "Constant"),   data.frame(time = t_mp, hazard = num_hazard(decomp$late, t_mp),              Phase = "Late"),   data.frame(time = t_mp, hazard = num_hazard(decomp$total, t_mp),              Phase = "Total") ) h_long$Phase <- factor(h_long$Phase,                        levels = c("Total", "Early", "Constant", "Late"))  ggplot(h_long, aes(time, hazard, colour = Phase, linetype = Phase)) +   geom_line(aes(linewidth = Phase)) +   scale_colour_manual(values = c(Total = "#222222", Early = "#E69F00",                                  Constant = "#56B4E9", Late = "#CC79A7")) +   scale_linetype_manual(values = c(Total = "solid", Early = "dashed",                                    Constant = "dashed", Late = "dashed")) +   scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(Total = 1.3, Early = 0.7,                                     Constant = 0.7, Late = 0.7)) +   labs(x = "Months after CABG", y = "Hazard rate",        colour = "Phase", linetype = "Phase", linewidth = "Phase") +   theme_minimal() +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

title: Migrating from SAS HAZARD to TemporalHazard
text: SAS HAZARD analysis stack statements inside PROC HAZARD block. walk roughly order appear typical analysis script, showing SAS form corresponding R call. procedure-level statement names dataset sets global options. NOCOV / NOCOR flags suppress covariance correlation output; CONDITION= tolerance switch convergence check. Maps hazard() control list: Additional PROC HAZARD options direct R equivalent yet passed ... named arguments stored fit$legacy_args. Names follow-time variable. SAS HAZARD separate statement; R ’s first argument Surv() inside formula. Maps directly time: Must non-negative numeric vector time unit original analysis (months, AVC example). Missing values permitted. Names event-indicator variable. Like TIME, separate statement SAS HAZARD enters R formula Surv(). Maps status: TemporalHazard coerces status numeric; logical vectors also accepted. HAZARD convention uses 1 = occurred, 0 = censored/alive last contact. Supplies starting values optimizer flags parameters hold fixed (FIXM, FIXMU, etc.). starting values matter — multiphase optimizer particular, poor starting point can park fit local minimum well away global MLE. Maps theta (coefficient/parameter vector) control (fix flags): Note: Full SAS PARMS syntax mirrored one--one public API. current package, supply parameter vector directly via theta record fixed-parameter intent control$fix. legacy parity helpers generate SAS-style control text comparing historical binaries. statements assign covariates specific phases. SAS HAZARD block lists covariates affect phase starting coefficients. Covariates can appear multiple blocks different starting values — column, different phase-specific effect. HAZARD, EARLY CONSTANT define phase-specific covariate coefficients. TemporalHazard unified single design matrix x coefficient vector theta M1. Phase assignment formalised M2 multi-phase likelihood implemented. Current convention (M1): combine covariates x supply corresponding starting coefficients theta. Triggers stepwise covariate selection inside hazard fit. SLE significance level entry, SLS staying. SAS HAZARD embedded PROC HAZARD call; R stepwise loop separate hzr_stepwise() function wraps fitted hazard() object. TemporalHazard now ships hzr_stepwise(), implements forward, backward, two-way stepwise selection SAS-style SLENTRY / SLSTAY thresholds, phase-specific entry multiphase models, MOVE oscillation guard. now defaults criterion = "score", reproduces SAS’s SELECTION Q statistic — score test current estimates, per-candidate refit — entry decisions match SAS’s directly. Passing criterion = "wald" selects older refit-based path, fits candidate testing . See ?hzr_stepwise full option list.
code: PROC HAZARD DATA=AVCS NOCOV NOCOR CONDITION=14; fit <- hazard(   ...,   control = list(     nocov      = TRUE,   # suppress covariance output     nocor      = TRUE,   # suppress correlation output     condition  = 14      # CONDITION= switch   ) ) TIME INT_DEAD; fit <- hazard(   time   = avcs$INT_DEAD,   ... ) EVENT DEAD; fit <- hazard(   status = avcs$DEAD,   # 1 = event, 0 = censored   ... ) PARMS MUE=0.3504743 THALF=0.1905077 NU=1.437416 M=1 FIXM       MUC=4.391673E-07; fit <- hazard(   theta   = c(MUE = 0.3504743, THALF = 0.1905077, NU = 1.437416,               M = 1,           MUC   = 4.391673e-07),   control = list(     fix = c("M")   # FIXM → freeze M during optimization   ),   ... ) EARLY  AGE=-0.03205774, COM_IV=1.336675, MAL=0.6872028,        OPMOS=-0.01963377, OP_AGE=0.0002086689, STATUS=0.5169533; CONSTANT INC_SURG=1.375285, ORIFICE=3.11765, STATUS=1.054988; # Build design matrix from the AVC data set X <- data.matrix(avcs[, c("AGE", "COM_IV", "MAL", "OPMOS", "OP_AGE",                            "STATUS", "INC_SURG", "ORIFICE")])  # Starting values from SAS EARLY + CONSTANT blocks combined theta_start <- c(   AGE      = -0.03205774,   COM_IV   =  1.336675,   MAL      =  0.6872028,   OPMOS    = -0.01963377,   OP_AGE   =  0.0002086689,   STATUS   =  0.5169533,   # EARLY phase coefficient   INC_SURG =  1.375285,   ORIFICE  =  3.11765 )  fit <- hazard(   time   = avcs$INT_DEAD,   status = avcs$DEAD,   x      = X,   theta  = theta_start,   dist   = "weibull" ) SELECTION SLE=0.2 SLS=0.1;

title: Migrating from SAS HAZARD to TemporalHazard
text: Statement--statement mapping fine reference, full gestalt lands see complete SAS HAZARD analysis R translation side side. example final multivariable model examples/hm.death.AVC.sas reference C repository — death atrioventricular canal repair, two-phase model covariates assigned specific phases. ’s canonical “real SAS HAZARD analysis looks like” specimen. original SAS code, exactly appears reference distribution. Notice statements stack inside single %HAZARD() macro call. model TemporalHazard. Every SAS statement corresponding R argument : TIME EVENT collapse Surv(int_dead, dead) left formula; global covariate list goes right; PARMS starting values become theta vector; phase-specific assignments use formula argument inside hzr_phase(); FIXM becomes fixed = "shapes" (subset shape names). line--line correspondence point — ’ve translated one analysis way, pattern carries every .
code: %HAZARD( PROC HAZARD DATA=AVCS P CONSERVE OUTHAZ=OUTEST CONDITION=14 QUASI;      TIME INT_DEAD;      EVENT DEAD;      PARMS MUE=0.3504743 THALF=0.1905077 NU=1.437416 M=1 FIXM            MUC=4.391673E-07;      EARLY   AGE=-0.03205774, COM_IV=1.336675,  MAL=0.6872028,              OPMOS=-0.01963377, OP_AGE=0.0002086689, STATUS=0.5169533;      CONSTANT INC_SURG=1.375285, ORIFICE=3.11765, STATUS=1.054988; ); # Assumed: avcs is a data.frame read from the AVC flat file # (same variables as the SAS DATA step)  avcs <- avcs |>   transform(     LN_AGE   = log(AGE),     LN_OPMOS = log(OPMOS),     LN_INC   = ifelse(is.na(INC_SURG), NA, log(INC_SURG + 1)),     LN_NYHA  = log(STATUS)   )  # Replace missing INC_SURG with column mean (mirrors PROC STANDARD REPLACE) avcs$INC_SURG[is.na(avcs$INC_SURG)] <- mean(avcs$INC_SURG, na.rm = TRUE)  X <- data.matrix(avcs[, c("AGE", "COM_IV", "MAL", "OPMOS", "OP_AGE",                            "STATUS", "INC_SURG", "ORIFICE")])  fit <- hazard(   time    = avcs$INT_DEAD,   status  = avcs$DEAD,   x       = X,   theta   = c(     # Hazard shape parameters (from PARMS)     MUE   = 0.3504743,     THALF = 0.1905077,     NU    = 1.437416,     M     = 1,     MUC   = 4.391673e-07,     # Covariate coefficients (from EARLY + CONSTANT blocks)     AGE      = -0.03205774,     COM_IV   =  1.336675,     MAL      =  0.6872028,     OPMOS    = -0.01963377,     OP_AGE   =  0.0002086689,     STATUS   =  0.5169533,     INC_SURG =  1.375285,     ORIFICE  =  3.11765   ),   dist    = "weibull",   control = list(     condition = 14,     quasi     = TRUE,     conserve  = TRUE,     fix       = c("M")   # FIXM   ) )  fit

title: Migrating from SAS HAZARD to TemporalHazard
text: SAS HAZARD veteran migrating TemporalHazard aware following scope limits v1.2.2. Detailed status per feature tracked inst/dev/SAS-PARITY-GAP-ANALYSIS.md inst/dev/DEVELOPMENT-PLAN.md. Supported: hzr_stepwise() implements forward / backward / two-way stepwise SAS-style SLENTRY / SLSTAY thresholds, per-phase entry multiphase, MOVE oscillation guard. yet supported: FAST-screening (Lawless-Singhal approximate Wald updates). Much exists save already gone, though: default criterion = "score" tests candidate current estimates never refits . criterion = "wald" still refits per entry candidate. Removals never , either criterion: drop tested current model’s Wald p-value slstay, SAS , accepted drop refitted. Supported: time_windows applies one piecewise-constant cut-point set across covariates. yet supported: distinct EARLY/LATE window sets per phase. Workaround: expand design matrix manually calling hazard(). R equivalents coef(fit) vcov(fit) memory; automatic dataset-export mode. saveRDS() need -disk artefact. predict.hazard() covers hazard, cumulative_hazard, survival, linear_predictor. Density quantile (median survival) types wired ; derive cumulative_hazard survival predictions needed. users migrating older TemporalHazard versions reading older SAS parity notes: weights distributions — shipped v0.9.6. Weibull, exponential, log-logistic, log-normal, multiphase honour observation weights end--end (LL + analytic gradient + multiphase Conservation Events). Surv(start, stop, event) start > 0 — shipped v0.9.7. Counting-process rows contribute H(stop) - H(start) Weibull multiphase. previous hazard() guard non-zero starts gone. Delta-method prediction confidence limits — shipped v0.9.8. Use predict(..., se.fit = TRUE, level = 0.95) get data frame fit, se.fit, lower, upper per row. Closed-form Jacobian Weibull multiphase, numDeriv::jacobian fallback exponential / log-logistic / log-normal.

code: # Three-phase additive hazard decomposition fit_mp <- hazard(   survival::Surv(int_dead, dead) ~ 1,   data   = cabgkul,   dist   = "multiphase",   phases = list(     early    = hzr_phase("cdf", t_half = 0.2, nu = 1, m = 1,                           fixed = "shapes"),     constant = hzr_phase("constant"),     late     = hzr_phase("g3",  tau = 1, gamma = 3, alpha = 1, eta = 1,                           fixed = "shapes")   ),   fit = TRUE ) summary(fit_mp)  # Per-phase decomposition of cumulative hazard t_grid <- seq(0.01, max(cabgkul$int_dead) * 0.9, length.out = 200) predict(fit_mp, newdata = data.frame(time = t_grid),         type = "cumulative_hazard", decompose = TRUE)

title: TemporalHazard: Temporal Parametric Hazard Modeling — TemporalHazard-package
text: total cumulative hazard decomposes additively across \(J\) phases: $$H(t \mid \mathbf{x}) = \sum_{j=1}^{J} \mu_j(\mathbf{x}) \,       \Phi_j(t)$$ \(\mu_j(\mathbf{x}) = \exp(\alpha_j + \mathbf{x}_j^\top \beta_j)\) phase-specific log-linear scale (intercept plus covariate effects) \(\Phi_j(t)\) temporal shape contributed phase \(j\), parameters depending phase type (see phase vocabulary ).  instantaneous hazard survival follow directly: $$h(t \mid \mathbf{x}) = \sum_{j=1}^{J} \mu_j(\mathbf{x}) \,       \varphi_j(t), \qquad       S(t \mid \mathbf{x}) = \exp\!\bigl(-H(t \mid \mathbf{x})\bigr)$$ \(\varphi_j = d\Phi_j/dt\).  phase specified hzr_phase() model fit maximum likelihood hazard().

Prediction predict() fitted hazard object — survival, cumulative hazard, per-phase decomposed hazard; summary() — coefficient tables Wald inference. "loglogistic" — unimodal (rise--fall) hazard log-logistic proportional-odds form (covariates act multiplicatively odds failure, \(\exp(\eta)\), AFT time shift) whose hazard rises single peak declines shape exceeds 1 (monotone decreasing otherwise), heavier tails log-normal.  Use risk climbs early peak eases . "lognormal" — early-peaking, resolving hazard accelerated-failure-time form \(\log\) time Gaussian; hazard rises early peak decays toward zero.  Use risk concentrated early resolves time. "multiphase" — additive N-phase hazard Sums several phase shapes one model, \(H = \sum_j \mu_j(\mathbf{x}) \Phi_j(t)\), overall hazard can fall, level , rise within one fit. Requires phases; see hzr_phase() available phase shapes.  form reproduces classic C/SAS HAZARD models.

title: Build and optionally fit a hazard model — hazard
code: # -- Univariable Weibull ---------------------------------------------- set.seed(1) time   <- rexp(50, rate = 0.3) status <- sample(0:1, 50, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.3, 0.7)) fit <- hazard(time = time, status = status,               theta = c(0.3, 1.0), dist = "weibull", fit = TRUE) summary(fit) #> hazard model summary #>   observations: 50  #>   predictors:   0  #>   dist:         weibull  #>   engine:       native-r-m2  #>   converged:    TRUE  #>   log-lik:      -89.5173  #>   evaluations: fn=23, gr=7 #>  #> Coefficients: #>     estimate  std_error   z_stat      p_value #> mu 0.2190092 0.02728228 8.027524 9.945983e-16 #> nu 1.3389540 0.15829050 8.458840 2.700510e-17  # -- Formula interface with covariates -------------------------------- set.seed(1001) n   <- 180 dat <- data.frame(   time   = rexp(n, rate = 0.35) + 0.05,   status = rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = 0.6),   age    = rnorm(n, mean = 62, sd = 11),   nyha   = sample(1:4, n, replace = TRUE),   shock  = rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = 0.18) )  fit2 <- hazard(   survival::Surv(time, status) ~ age + nyha + shock,   data    = dat,   theta   = c(mu = 0.25, nu = 1.10, beta1 = 0, beta2 = 0, beta3 = 0),   dist    = "weibull",   fit     = TRUE,   control = list(maxit = 300) ) summary(fit2) #> hazard model summary #>   observations: 180  #>   predictors:   3  #>   dist:         weibull  #>   engine:       native-r-m2  #>   converged:    TRUE  #>   log-lik:      -293.553  #>   evaluations: fn=36, gr=8 #>  #> Coefficients: #>          estimate   std_error      z_stat      p_value #> mu    0.121860518 0.062260593  1.95726560 5.031625e-02 #> nu    1.143730632 0.084302528 13.56697905 6.285984e-42 #> beta1 0.001716551 0.008807986  0.19488579 8.454824e-01 #> beta2 0.156208724 0.090597558  1.72420458 8.467092e-02 #> beta3 0.017352702 0.362918430  0.04781433 9.618642e-01  # \donttest{ # -- Parametric survival with Kaplan-Meier overlay ----------------- if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {   library(ggplot2)    # Parametric curve on a fine grid at median covariate profile   t_grid   <- seq(0.05, max(dat$time), length.out = 80)   curve_df <- data.frame(     time = t_grid, age = median(dat$age), nyha = 2, shock = 0   )   curve_df$survival <- predict(fit2, newdata = curve_df,                                type = "survival") * 100    # Kaplan-Meier empirical overlay   km    <- survival::survfit(survival::Surv(time, status) ~ 1, data = dat)   km_df <- data.frame(time = km$time, survival = km$surv * 100)    ggplot() +     geom_step(data = km_df, aes(time, survival, colour = "Kaplan-Meier")) +     geom_line(data = curve_df, aes(time, survival,                                    colour = "Parametric (Weibull)")) +     scale_colour_manual(       values = c("Parametric (Weibull)" = "#0072B2",                  "Kaplan-Meier"         = "#D55E00")     ) +     scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +     labs(x = "Months after surgery", y = "Freedom from death (%)",          colour = NULL) +     theme_minimal() +     theme(legend.position = "bottom") }  # }  # \donttest{ # -- Multiphase model (two phases) --------------------------------- fit_mp <- hazard(   survival::Surv(time, status) ~ 1,   data   = dat,   dist   = "multiphase",   phases = list(     early = hzr_phase("cdf", t_half = 0.5, nu = 2, m = 0,                        fixed = "shapes"),     late  = hzr_phase("cdf", t_half = 5,   nu = 1, m = 0,                        fixed = "shapes")   ),   fit     = TRUE,   control = list(n_starts = 5, maxit = 1000) ) summary(fit_mp) #> Multiphase hazard model (2 phases) #>   observations: 180  #>   predictors:   0  #>   dist:         multiphase  #>   phase 1:      early - cdf (early risk) #>   phase 2:      late - cdf (late risk) #>   engine:       native-r-m2  #>   converged:    TRUE  #>   log-lik:      -321.926  #>   evaluations: fn=21, gr=6 #>  #> Coefficients (internal scale): #>  #>   Phase: early (cdf) #>                estimate std_error    z_stat      p_value #>   log_mu     -1.8214603  0.270271 -6.739385 1.590589e-11 #>   log_t_half -0.6931472        NA        NA           NA #>   nu          2.0000000        NA        NA           NA #>   m           0.0000000        NA        NA           NA #>  #>   Phase: late (cdf) #>               estimate std_error   z_stat     p_value #>   log_mu     0.6120246 0.1098426 5.571832 2.52075e-08 #>   log_t_half 1.6094379        NA       NA          NA #>   nu         1.0000000        NA       NA          NA #>   m          0.0000000        NA       NA          NA  # -- Per-phase decomposed cumulative hazard ------------------------ if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {   t_grid <- seq(0.01, max(dat$time), length.out = 100)   decomp <- predict(fit_mp, newdata = data.frame(time = t_grid),                     type = "cumulative_hazard", decompose = TRUE)    df_long <- data.frame(     time = rep(decomp$time, 3),     cumhaz = c(decomp$total, decomp$early, decomp$late),     component = rep(c("Total", "Early (cdf)", "Late (cdf)"),                     each = nrow(decomp))   )   df_long$component <- factor(df_long$component,     levels = c("Total", "Early (cdf)", "Late (cdf)"))    ggplot2::ggplot(df_long,     ggplot2::aes(x = time, y = cumhaz, colour = component,                  linewidth = component)) +     ggplot2::geom_line() +     ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = c(       "Total" = "black", "Early (cdf)" = "#0072B2",       "Late (cdf)" = "#D55E00"     )) +     ggplot2::scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(       "Total" = 1.2, "Early (cdf)" = 0.6, "Late (cdf)" = 0.6     )) +     ggplot2::labs(       x = "Time", y = "Cumulative hazard H(t)",       colour = NULL, linewidth = NULL,       title = "Multiphase decomposition: early + late"     ) +     ggplot2::theme_minimal() +     ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom") }  # }

title: Kaplan-Meier survival with exact logit confidence limits — hzr_kaplan
text: data frame one row per time point columns: time Event/censoring time. n_risk Number risk start interval. n_event Number events time. n_censor Number censored time. survival Kaplan-Meier survival estimate. std_err Standard error survival (Greenwood). cl_lower Lower confidence limit (logit-transformed). cl_upper Upper confidence limit (logit-transformed). cumhaz Cumulative hazard \(= -\log(S)\). hazard Interval hazard rate \(= \log(S_{t-1} / S_t) / \Delta t\). density Probability density estimate \(= (S_{t-1} - S_t) / \Delta t\). life Restricted mean survival time (area curve time).

title: Kaplan-Meier survival with exact logit confidence limits — hzr_kaplan
text: standard Greenwood confidence interval can exceed \([0, 1]\) tails. logit-transformed interval avoids working log-odds scale: $$   \text{CL}_{\text{lower}} = S / \bigl(S + (1-S)\,   \exp(z_\alpha\,\text{SI})\bigr) $$ $$   \text{CL}_{\text{upper}} = S / \bigl(S + (1-S)\,   \exp(-z_\alpha\,\text{SI})\bigr) $$ \(\text{SI} = \sqrt{V_P - 1} / (1 - S)\), \(V_P\) cumulative Greenwood variance product, \(z_\alpha\) normal quantile requested confidence level.

text: Computes "softplus" function $$\mathrm{log1pexp}(x) = \log\!\bigl(1 + e^{x}\bigr)$$ without overflow.  naive log(1 + exp(x)) overflows Inf \(x \gtrsim 710\) even though true value \(\approx x\).  identity \(\log(1 + e^{x}) = x + \log(1 + e^{-x})\) \(x > 0\) keeps every intermediate finite.

title: Specify a single hazard phase — hzr_phase
text: type Character; phase's temporal shape — one "cdf" (early resolving risk), "hazard" (accumulating G1 aging risk), "g3" (late rising risk, original C/SAS late phase), "constant" (flat background rate).  See Phase types section means use . t_half Positive scalar; initial half-life (time \(G(t_{1/2}) = 0.5\)).  Used "cdf" "hazard" phases. SAS early: THALF/RHO. nu Numeric scalar; initial time exponent.  Used "cdf" "hazard" phases.  SAS early: NU. m Numeric scalar; initial shape exponent.  Used "cdf" "hazard" phases.  SAS early: M. tau Positive scalar; scale parameter "g3" phases. SAS late: TAU. gamma Positive scalar; time exponent "g3" phases. SAS late: GAMMA. alpha Non-negative scalar; shape parameter "g3" phases. alpha > 0, generic G3 formula used; alpha = 0 gives exponential limiting case.  SAS late: ALPHA. eta Positive scalar; outer exponent "g3" phases. SAS late: ETA. formula Optional one-sided formula (e.g. ~ age + nyha) phase-specific covariates.  NULL (default), phase inherits global formula hazard(). fixed Character vector naming shape parameters hold fixed optimization.  Valid names "cdf"/"hazard": "t_half", "nu", "m", "shapes" (shorthand three).  Valid names "g3": "tau", "gamma", "alpha", "eta", "shapes" (shorthand four).  Fixed parameters held starting values; mu (covariates) estimated.  Ignored "constant" phases. mirrors SAS/C HAZARD workflow shapes typically fixed scale parameters estimated. x hzr_phase object (print.hzr_phase()). ... Additional arguments (ignored).

title: Specify a single hazard phase — hzr_phase
text: S3 object class "hzr_phase" elements: type Phase type string. t_half Initial half-life (cdf/hazard phases). nu Initial time exponent (cdf/hazard phases). m Initial shape exponent (cdf/hazard phases). tau Scale parameter (g3 phases). gamma Time exponent (g3 phases). alpha Shape parameter (g3 phases). eta Outer exponent (g3 phases). formula Phase-specific formula NULL. fixed Character vector fixed parameter names (may empty).

title: Specify a single hazard phase — hzr_phase
text: phase one term \(j\) additive cumulative hazard $$H(t \mid \mathbf{x}) = \sum_{j=1}^{J} \mu_j(\mathbf{x}) \,       \Phi_j(t)$$ \(\mu_j(\mathbf{x}) = \exp(\alpha_j + \mathbf{x}_j^\top \beta_j)\) phase-specific log-linear scale \(\Phi_j(t)\) temporal shape selected type ().  t_half/nu/m (g3 tau/gamma/alpha/eta) arguments set starting values shape; formula attaches covariates \(\mathbf{x}_j\) enter \(\mu_j\).

title: Specify a single hazard phase — hzr_phase
text: type argument chooses temporal shape \(\Phi_j(t)\) phase. captures qualitatively different pattern risk time; typical clinical model combines early, constant, late phase total hazard can fall, level , rise . "cdf" — early, resolving risk Named cumulative distribution function: phase contributes \(\Phi(t) = G(t)\), bounded CDF temporal decomposition (\(0\) \(t = 0\), rising ceiling \(1\)).  saturates, hazard adds, \(\mu\,g(t)\), peaks early decays toward zero — signature one-time insult patients either succumb survive past, e.g. peri-operative mortality.  Shape set t_half, nu, m. SAS/C equivalent: Early (G1) phase. "hazard" — accumulating aging risk (G1 family) Named phase contributes cumulative hazard built G1 family: \(\Phi(t) = -\log(1 - G(t))\), unbounded monotone increasing.  hazard \(\mu\,h(t)\) rises without leveling , models risk grows subjects age.  alternative late-risk form derived G1; original SAS/C late phase prefer "g3". Shape set t_half, nu, m. "g3" — late, rising risk (original C/SAS late phase) Named G3 (third) decomposition family used original HAZARD program late phase.  contributes \(\Phi(t) = G_3(t)\) hzr_decompos_g3(), unbounded intensity four-parameter shape (tau, gamma, alpha, eta) flexible G1-derived "hazard" form capturing accelerating late mortality (e.g. structural valve deterioration years surgery).  Use reproducing classic three-phase HAZARD models.  SAS/C equivalent: Late (G3) phase. "constant" — flat background rate time-invariant hazard: \(\Phi(t) = t\), added hazard \(\mu\) constant (exponential model).  represents steady, ongoing risk present follow-times, independent long ago time origin .  Takes shape parameters — scale \(\mu\) (covariates) estimated.  SAS/C equivalent: Constant (G2) phase. shape derivative \(\varphi_j = d\Phi_j/dt\) (forms instantaneous hazard contribution \(\mu_j\,\varphi_j(t)\)) \(g(t)\) "cdf", \(h(t)\) "hazard", \(g_3(t)\) "g3", \(1\) "constant".

title: Specify a single hazard phase — hzr_phase
code: # Classic 3-phase Blackstone pattern early <- hzr_phase("cdf",      t_half = 0.5, nu = 2, m = 0) const <- hzr_phase("constant") late  <- hzr_phase("g3", tau = 1, gamma = 3, alpha = 1, eta = 1)  # Fix all shapes (C/SAS-style: only estimate mu) early_fixed <- hzr_phase("cdf", t_half = 0.5, nu = 2, m = 0,                           fixed = "shapes") late_fixed  <- hzr_phase("g3", tau = 1, gamma = 3, alpha = 1, eta = 1,                           fixed = "shapes")  # Fix only some parameters early_partial <- hzr_phase("cdf", t_half = 0.5, nu = 2, m = 0,                             fixed = c("nu", "m"))  # Phase with specific covariates early_cov <- hzr_phase("cdf", t_half = 0.5, nu = 2, m = 0,                         formula = ~ age + shock)  # Use in hazard(): # hazard(Surv(time, status) ~ age, data = dat, #        dist = "multiphase", #        phases = list(early = early, constant = const, late = late))

text: time Numeric vector times (> 0). t_half Half-life parameter (> 0). nu Time exponent. m Shape parameter. type Phase type: "cdf" (early – uses \(G(t)\)), "hazard" (late – uses cumulative hazard \(h(t)\)), "constant" (flat rate – \(\Phi = t\)).

title: Cumulative hazard contribution from a single phase — hzr_phase_cumhaz
text: "cdf": \(\Phi(t) = G(t)\).  Bounded \([0, 1]\).  Models early risk resolves time. "hazard": \(\Phi(t) = -\log(1 - G(t))\).  Monotone increasing. Models late aging risk.  cumulative hazard derived hazard function \(h(t)\), since \(\int_0^t h(s)\,ds = -\log(1 - G(t))\). "constant": \(\Phi(t) = t\).  Ignores t_half, nu, m. Equivalent exponential (constant hazard rate).

title: Stepwise covariate selection for a parametric hazard model — hzr_stepwise
text: Two arguments shape search.  direction decides moves allowed step; criterion decides candidate move scored whether accepted. direction = "forward" Start base model add variables — best eligible candidate enters step none clears entry rule.  Variables never leave . direction = "backward" Start full candidate model drop variables — weakest term leaves step survivors clear retention rule. direction = "" (default) Two-way stepwise: entry, already-selected variables re-tested may dropped. SAS SELECTION = STEPWISE strategy.  max_move caps often single variable may oscillate frozen. criterion = "score" (default) Accept moves SAS-style significance thresholds, using score (Q) statistic candidate coefficient — reproduces C/SAS HAZARD's SELECTION statistic. Q evaluated current model's MLE candidate's coefficient pinned zero, candidate refit needed: reduced-model information inverted per step reused across every candidate.  winner refit.  candidate enters p-value slentry. Score entry criterion; drop path never refit per candidate first place, removals tested current model's Wald p-value slstay, SAS . single-distribution fits, score criterion computes observed information numerically via suggested numDeriv package errors clear message installed; multiphase fit uses analytic Hessian instead need . Following SAS, variance used selection approximate: shaping-parameter covariances ignored.  affects selection — final-model standard errors unchanged still come full Hessian.  Candidates must single-column numeric main-effect terms; factor rejected error rather skipped. criterion = "wald" Accept moves SAS-style significance thresholds, using Wald \(\chi^2\) affected coefficient(s): candidate enters p-value slentry, term dropped p-value rises slstay.  Entry candidates scored refit adds candidate (new coefficient can tested); drop candidates scored current model's Wald p-values without per-candidate refit, single refit run drop chosen.  default version 1.2.0. differs algorithmically C/SAS HAZARD, two criteria can take different step paths — select different variable sets — even converge similar final model. criterion = "aic" Accept move \(\Delta\mathrm{AIC} < 0\) (strictly better penalised fit), ignoring slentry / slstay.  Entry candidates use actual \(\Delta\mathrm{AIC}\) candidate refit; drop candidates use Wald--likelihood-ratio approximation, \(\Delta\mathrm{AIC} \approx W - 2\,\mathrm{df}\), computed current model without per-candidate refit (chosen drop refit afterwards).  Use non-significance-based, information-criterion search.

Ignored single-distribution models.  Default FALSE. se.fit Logical; TRUE, compute delta-method standard errors confidence limits prediction.  return value becomes data frame columns fit, se.fit, lower, upper.  Default FALSE. CLs computed log-hazard / log-cumhaz scale log(-log(survival)) scale lower/upper stay inside valid range prediction type; linear_predictor uses symmetric natural-scale CLs. multiphase models, se.fit = TRUE combines decompose = TRUE type = "cumulative_hazard": result long data frame one row per prediction time component (component "total" plus phase name) columns fit, se.fit, lower, upper. Per-phase CLs use phase's parameters, sum total CL. combination available type = "survival" (per-phase survival additive). level Numeric confidence level (0, 1); default 0.95. used se.fit = TRUE. text: predict.hazard(type = "hazard") now works multiphase models, returning instantaneous additive hazard h(t|x) = sum_j mu_j(x) phi_j'(t) (previously single-distribution models supported "hazard", via exp(eta)). Like "survival" / "cumulative_hazard" time-based (requires newdata$time), supports covariate newdata, se.fit = TRUE (delta-method limits log scale via numeric Jacobian hazard evaluator). decompose = TRUE supported "hazard". gives multiphase instantaneous hazard public route (previously reachable internal functions). predict.hazard(..., se.fit = TRUE, conf.type = "logit") selects survival confidence-limit transform. default "log-log" builds limits log(-log S) (survival::survfit standard); "logit" builds logit(1 - S), reproducing SAS HAZARD’s HAZPRED survival limits. full-information vcov CoE fits, conf.type = "logit" matches SAS hp.death.AVC survival CLs ~1e-5. Hazard / cumulative-hazard limits unaffected (log scale already matches HAZPRED). predict.hazard(type = "cumulative_hazard", decompose = TRUE, se.fit = TRUE) now returns per-phase total delta-method confidence limits multiphase models, long data frame (time, component, fit, se.fit, lower, upper). phase’s CL uses phase’s parameters, per-phase limits sum total. Previously combination raised error.

title: TemporalHazard 1.1.0
text: Hardened Hessian inversion standard errors (Phase 7c). Post-fit variance-covariance estimation now symmetrizes Hessian, checks reciprocal condition number, inverts via Cholesky solve() fallback non-positive-definite Hessians, guards non-positive variances instead silently emitting NaN standard errors. Ill-conditioned, non-positive-definite, non-finite Hessians now raise specific, named warnings, fits carry rcond / pd diagnostics summary() surfaces note fit flagged. closes “12+-parameter Hessian stability” hardening item inversion layer; analytic Hessians (accurate standard errors) follow subsequent releases. Analytic Hessian exponential standard errors (Phase 7c, Layer 2). exponential distribution now computes post-fit Hessian closed form (X~' diag(wH) X~ event + right-censored rows) rather numerically, giving accurate standard errors. shared optimizer gained hessian_fn hook analytic Hessians remaining families reuse; left/interval-censored exponential fits fall back numerical Hessian. Analytic Hessian Weibull standard errors (Phase 7c, Layer 2). Weibull distribution now computes post-fit Hessian closed form internal (alpha, psi, beta) optimization scale (mapped natural scale existing delta method) rather numerically, giving accurate standard errors. Covers event + right-censored data (including counting-process start times); left/interval-censored fits fall back numerical Hessian. Analytic Hessian log-logistic standard errors (Phase 7c, Layer 2). log-logistic distribution now computes post-fit Hessian closed form internal (log alpha, log beta, beta_coef) scale rather numerically, giving accurate standard errors. Covers event + right-censored data; left/interval-censored fits fall back numerical Hessian. Analytic Hessian log-normal standard errors (Phase 7c, Layer 2). log-normal distribution now computes post-fit Hessian closed form internal (mu, log_sigma, beta_coef) scale rather numerically, giving accurate standard errors. Covers event + right-censored data; left/interval-censored fits fall back numerical Hessian. Analytic Hessian multiphase standard errors (Phase 7c, Layer 2 PR-6). Post-fit standard errors multiphase fits now come closed-form Hessian negative log-likelihood rather numerical Richardson approximation. Hessian assembled three terms: () phase-block-diagonal curvature Σᵢ wᵢ H(tᵢ), (B) dense Fisher information outer product Σₑ (wᵢ/hᵢ²) ∇h ∇hᵀ capturing cross-phase parameter interactions, (C) phase-block-diagonal curvature −Σₑ wᵢ log h(tᵢ). μ/β parameters use fully closed-form expressions; shape parameters (t_half, ν, m, G3 parameters) use second-order central differences. Conservation--Events full-information vcov path also switches analytic Hessian. Left/interval-censored fits fall back numerical Hessian. Completes 6-PR analytic-Hessian rollout across five families.

title: TemporalHazard 0.9.3
text: hzr_deciles() — Decile--risk calibration function comparing observed vs. expected event counts across risk groups chi-square GOF testing. Implements SAS deciles.hazard.sas macro workflow. hzr_gof() — Goodness--fit function comparing parametric predictions nonparametric (Kaplan-Meier) estimates observed vs. expected event counting. Implements SAS hazplot.sas macro workflow. hzr_kaplan() — Kaplan-Meier survival estimator logit-transformed confidence limits respect [0, 1] boundary, interval hazard rate, density, restricted mean survival time (life integral). Implements SAS kaplan.sas macro output structure. hzr_calibrate() — Variable calibration function assessing functional form model entry. Groups continuous covariate quantile bins applies logit, Gompertz, Cox link transforms. Supports stratification via parameter. Implements SAS logit.sas logitgr.sas macros. hzr_nelson() — Wayne Nelson cumulative hazard estimator lognormal confidence limits. Supports weighted events severity-adjusted repeated event analyses. Implements SAS nelsonl.sas macro. hzr_bootstrap() — Bootstrap resampling hazard model coefficients bagging support (fractional sampling). Returns per-replicate estimates summary statistics (mean, SD, percentile CI). Implements SAS bootstrap.hazard.sas macro workflow. hzr_competing_risks() — Competing risks cumulative incidence using Aalen-Johansen estimator Greenwood variance. Handles number competing event types. Implements SAS markov.sas macro. Conservation Events (CoE) — Turner’s theorem now integrated multiphase optimizer. One phase’s log_mu scaling parameter solved analytically iteration, reducing optimization dimension 1 improving numerical stability convergence. Enabled default; disable control = list(conserve = FALSE). Implements core algorithm C HAZARD setcoe.c / consrv.c. text: Multiphase engine: N-phase additive cumulative hazard models via dist = "multiphase" hzr_phase() specification. hzr_decompos() parametric family implementing three-parameter temporal decomposition Blackstone, Naftel, Turner (1986). Multi-start optimizer Hessian-based variance-covariance estimation. C binary parity tests KUL CABG reference dataset. Five clinical reference datasets: avc, cabgkul, omc, tga, valves.

title: TemporalHazard 0.1.0
text: Single-phase engine: Weibull, exponential, log-logistic, log-normal distributions formula interface. hazard() API predict(), summary(), coef(), vcov() S3 methods. Golden fixture regression testing system. Numerically stable helper primitives (hzr_log1pexp, hzr_log1mexp, hzr_clamp_prob).

title: TemporalHazard 0.0.0.9000
